I don't know how much of a valid point of view i have on all that, but still

In my opinion, the whole business with Makoto is that she's slowly but surely getting disconnected from her own life and losing her way, day in and day out, with sensei being one of the last things that still had value. And with him doing a 180 as well, it may or may not have lethal effects on her own, already struggling, mental state.
That said, i can tell you that people which decide to end their own life very rarely do it out of spite for anybody, and also it's rarely an action that is aimed at detrimenting their dearest/whoever is nearby at that moment. Moments like the one on top of the world roof is, rudely said, a selfish attempt at making peace with whatever is one's problem at that time, whichever solution the person in question is trying to come to terms with. Sometimes it's an equivalent at holding your most valued thing in your hands for the last time, or hearing your most loved person before you go. If you are already going, you want your last thing to remember before darkness to be a happy one.

Talking about this specific instance between sensei and Makoto, i think she was just in a bad spot that evening and needed to calm down, before finding sensei in the hallway and deciding the one light that's still hanging in her life is not a bad thing to have around on the roof. It was only after the conversation when the thought clicked in her mind that it's enough, then and there. Now i'm not saying she wouldn't do it if sensei wasn't there that evening, but something tells me that him being there is what give her the out. Making peace with the option that she chose on that roof, if you want it that way. The final piece that tipped the scales to the other side, the "yeah, it's better that way" thought. You know.

But after all, that's just my speculation. The truth lies only with Selebus. Maybe one day he'll tell us what was happening with her throughout the story and on that very evening.

It seems to me more like it was a spur of the moment thing. She wasn't thinking of it as a way to screw over anyone, just as a way to escape. Remember at the start of the event she was going out on her own. It was just luck that she ran into Sensei. My guess is she let him come along hoping he could help her feel better precisely because she looks up to him.

I only semi-saw it coming. I saw several signs that she was struggling in her interactions leading up to that event, but I didn't make the full connection until the event had already started. But it makes sense that it would be difficult to see coming. As I said in an earlier post, I was in a very similar situation to Makoto many years ago, even having suicidal thoughts. However, I hid it very well from most people. Years after the fact, I talked with some of my close friends I had back then, and they all confirmed they had no idea I was even depressed, let alone suicidal at the time. Only person who saw it was my mother who I lived with at the time and was a psychologist. If you don't know the signs, it can be super hard to spot.

One last thing. If whoever is reading this is struggling, but thinks other people's problems are worse, and it's not worth bothering others, so you can't bring yourself to ask for help; stop that thought process. Your problems are just as valid as anyone else's and there is nothing wrong with needing help, even if its embarrassing. The small problems can be some of the hardest to overcome since it's so hard to ask for help with them. You're worth helping though, so please reach out for it.

More Makoto
It seems to me more like it was a spur of the moment thing. She wasn't thinking of it as a way to screw over anyone, just as a way to escape. One last thing. If whoever is reading this is struggling, but thinks other people's problems are worse, and it's not worth bothering others, so you can't bring yourself to ask for help; stop that thought process. Your problems are just as valid as anyone else's and there is nothing wrong with needing help, even if its embarrassing. The small problems can be some of the hardest to overcome since it's so hard to ask for help with them. You're worth helping though, so please reach out for it.

Popletalko said:
I don't know how much of a valid point of view i have on all that, but still

In my opinion, the whole business with Makoto is that she's slowly but surely getting disconnected from her own life and losing her way, day in and day out, with sensei being one of the last things that still had value. And with him doing a 180 as well, it may or may not have lethal effects on her own, already struggling, mental state.
That said, i can tell you that people which decide to end their own life very rarely do it out of spite for anybody, and also it's rarely an action that is aimed at detrimenting their dearest/whoever is nearby at that moment. Moments like the one on top of the world roof is, rudely said, a selfish attempt at making peace with whatever is one's problem at that time, whichever solution the person in question is trying to come to terms with. Sometimes it's an equivalent at holding your most valued thing in your hands for the last time, or hearing your most loved person before you go. If you are already going, you want your last thing to remember before darkness to be a happy one.

Talking about this specific instance between sensei and Makoto, i think she was just in a bad spot that evening and needed to calm down, before finding sensei in the hallway and deciding the one light that's still hanging in her life is not a bad thing to have around on the roof. It was only after the conversation when the thought clicked in her mind that it's enough, then and there. Now i'm not saying she wouldn't do it if sensei wasn't there that evening, but something tells me that him being there is what give her the out. Making peace with the option that she chose on that roof, if you want it that way. The final piece that tipped the scales to the other side, the "yeah, it's better that way" thought. You know.

But after all, that's just my speculation. The truth lies only with Selebus. Maybe one day he'll tell us what was happening with her throughout the story and on that very evening.
Click to expand...
Based on how it played out, I don't even think it actually happened. It shows her doing it, then switches to her just sitting as she was before. If it had actually taken place, you would think she would be unable to be sitting there after if not having a scene where Sensei stops her at the last second after the jump takes place so that she could be. Either one or the other would have to happen for her to be sitting there afterwards to make sense. There's also the possibility that Sensei snapped, not hard when you literally just watched a girl jump to her death right in front of you.

Note: The game contains a myriad of Japanese terms, emoticons, small signs and various gadgets that make the translator extremely difficult as well as the correction routines. I believe it deserves the last place in the hit-parade of translations.

The link is: Mega

The translation is provided in two formats: .exe (self-extracting) and .zip. It is not necessary to use both.

It is the "raw" translation of files without grammatical corrections, often indispensable.
From time to time I will publish revisions which, in addition to the grammar, will correct the errors/omissions.

Installation (.exe format):
------------
1) Copy the translation file to the same directory where the main game file resides.
Example: You have a "HurryUp" game installed in "C:\Games\HurryUp". In this folder you will find the main file of the game called "HurryUp.exe". (Note: In PCs where extensions are not shown.) known files, this file will only result "HurryUp" of "Type" as "Application").
In this way, in the "C:\Games\HurryUp" folder there will be both the main file of game that of translation.
2) Launch the translation file and check that in the "Destination folder" selection box the game folder appears. In our example there must be "C:\Games\HurryUp". If not, it is necessary to modify the writing so that there is "C:\Games\HurryUp". Then click on "Extract".
3) At the end you can delete the translation file.
4) To verify that the translation has been installed correctly, check that the file is there zzz.rpy in the "game" folder of the game (In our example in "C:\Games\HurryUp\game") and that there is the "it" folder in "game\tl" (In our example in "C:\Games\HurryUp\game\tl").

P.S. If you cannot/want to copy the translation file to the game directory, just indicate the latter ("C:\Games\HurryUp") in the "Destination folder" selection box after launching the translation.
P.S.2 At the first start the game must integrate the translation files for which it will be necessary to wait patiently until this operation ends. This operation is done only at the first start.

Installation (.zip format):
------------
1) Copy the translation file to the same directory where the main game file resides.
Example: You have a "HurryUp" game installed in "C:\Games\HurryUp". In this folder you will find the main file of the game called "HurryUp.exe". (Note: In PCs where extensions are not shown.) known files, this file will only result "HurryUp" of "Type" as "Application").
In this way, in the "C:\Games\HurryUp" folder there will be both the main file of game that of translation.
2) Unzip the translation file.
3) At the end you can delete the translation file.
4) To verify that the translation has been installed correctly, check that the file is there zzz.rpy in the "game" folder of the game (In our example in "C:\Games\HurryUp\game") and that there is the "it" folder in "game\tl" (In our example in "C:\Games\HurryUp\game\tl").

Manual:
------
A small manual illustrated with installation instructions, in .pdf format, can be found here: Mega

Error Reporting:
---------------
If the game has crashes / errors / anomalies, please send me, in private, the log.txt, error.txt and traceback.txt files that are generated in the folder where is the executable file of the game (Note: Not all three of these files are always present) to be able to fix things...

Manual translation activation:
-----------------------------
In games where the choice of language is initially set, the Italian language activation setting is canceled by this choice. In this type of games, choose a language and, only after this, press the F12 key. If you want to return to the original game language, press ALT-F12 keys.

F.A.Q:
-----
* The menus are in Italian but the dialogues are in English. *
This condition sometimes occurs when using translation in a compressed game. Often, in fact, the compression of the game's images also involves the modification of the unique keys of the dialogues, making the translation unusable. The menus do not have unique keys and therefore are not subject to this anomaly.

* In dialogues the male and female gender are wrong or reversed. *
English is a language that often brings together genres. The phrase "Are you tired?" can be translated as "Sei stanca?" that "Sei stanco?". The correct gender attribution occurs only by analyzing the context of the sentence. Automatic translators practically always translate in the masculine. A total manual overhaul, line by line, would be required in order to correct all these errors. This work, both in terms of size and times, is considered too heavy and therefore is not carried out. However, the revision of dialogues through a series of neural network procedures mitigates these errors. It is the only additional work that is put in place and it is the translator's responsibility to constantly improve these procedures to refine the work more and more.

* The dialogues of some games contain incomprehensible acronyms. *
Unfortunately, some game developers use slang in dialogues. These "cripples" make machine translation difficult and, often, incomprehensible the acronyms that, in the original, should mean something in a contracted form. In one game there was the abbreviation "BBRGeem". Nobody, and I repeat nobody, of my American friends knows this acronym and, above all, its meaning.

* Translation implants the game *
Before making this statement it is necessary to verify that the game does not settle in the same point WITHOUT the translation. In this case, then, it can depend on a variable contained in the dialogue which, even if it is "screened" by automatic translation, this is modified. A typical variable is the player's name.
***********************************************************************

Tuttavia la revisione dei dialoghi attraverso una serie di procedure in rete neurale, attenua questi errori. E' il solo lavoro aggiuntivo che viene posto in essere ed e' cura del traduttore migliorare costantemente queste procedure per affinare sempre' piu' il lavoro.

Putroppo alcuni sviluppatori di giochi utilizzano lo slang nei dialoghi. In un gioco c'era la sigla "BBRGeem". Nessuno, e ripeto nessuno, dei miei amici americani conosce questa sigla e, soprattutto, il suo significato.

* La traduzione impianta il gioco. *
Prima di fare questa affermazione occorre verificare che il gioco non si impianti nello stesso punto SENZA la traduzione. In questo caso, allora, puo' dipendere da una variabile contenuta del dialogo che, pur avendola "schermata" alla traduzione automatica, questa viene modificata. Una tipica variabile e' il nome del giocatore.
E se questa traduzione vi piace, non dimenticate di mettere un Like, sempre ben accetto!

Often, in fact, the compression of the game's images also involves the modification of the unique keys of the dialogues, making the translation unusable. The menus do not have unique keys and therefore are not subject to this anomaly.

* In dialogues the male and female gender are wrong or reversed. *
English is a language that often brings together genres. The phrase "Are you tired?" can be translated as "Sei stanca?" that "Sei stanco?". The correct gender attribution occurs only by analyzing the context of the sentence. Automatic translators practically always translate in the masculine. A total manual overhaul, line by line, would be required in order to correct all these errors. This work, both in terms of size and times, is considered too heavy and therefore is not carried out. However, the revision of dialogues through a series of neural network procedures mitigates these errors. It is the only additional work that is put in place and it is the translator's responsibility to constantly improve these procedures to refine the work more and more.

* The dialogues of some games contain incomprehensible acronyms. *
Unfortunately, some game developers use slang in dialogues. These "cripples" make machine translation difficult and, often, incomprehensible the acronyms that, in the original, should mean something in a contracted form. In one game there was the abbreviation "BBRGeem". Nobody, and I repeat nobody, of my American friends knows this acronym and, above all, its meaning.

* Translation implants the game *
Before making this statement it is necessary to verify that the game does not settle in the same point WITHOUT the translation. In this case, then, it can depend on a variable contained in the dialogue which, even if it is "screened" by automatic translation, this is modified. A typical variable is the player's name.

spoilers.html:
E' la traduzione "grezza" dei file senza correzioni grammaticali, spesso indispensabili.
Di tanto in tanto pubblicherò delle revisioni che, oltre la grammatica, aggiusteranno gli errori/omissioni.

Installazione (formato .exe):
-------------
1) Copiare il file della traduzione nella stessa directory dove risiede il file principale del gioco.
Esempio: Si abbia un gioco "HurryUp" installato in "C:\Giochi\HurryUp". In questa cartella si troverà il file principale del gioco chiamato "HurryUp.exe". (Nota: Nei PC dove non sono mostrate le estensioni dei file noti, questo file risulterà solo "HurryUp" di "Tipo" come "Applicazione").
Così facendo, nella cartella "C:\Giochi\HurryUp" saranno presenti SIA il file principale del gioco CHE quello della traduzione.
2) Lanciare il file della traduzione e verificare che nella casella di selezione "Cartella di destinazione" compaia la cartella del gioco. Nel nostro esempio dovrà esserci "C:\Giochi\HurryUp". Se così non fosse, occorre modificare la scritta perchè ci sia "C:\Giochi\HurryUp". Dopo cliccare su "Estrai".
3) Al termine si potrà cancellare il file della traduzione.
4) Per verificare che la traduzione sia stata installata correttamente, verificare che ci sia il file zzz.rpy nella cartella "game" del gioco (Nel nostro esempio in "C:\Giochi\HurryUp\game") e che ci sia la cartella "it" in "game/tl" (Nel nostro esempio in "C:\Giochi\HurryUp\game\tl").

P.S. Qualora non si possa/voglia copiare il file della traduzione nella directory del gioco, basterà indicare quest'ultima ("C:\Giochi\HurryUp") nella casella di selezione "Cartella di destinazione" dopo aver lanciato la traduzione.
P.S. 2 Al primo avvio il gioco dovrà integrare i file della traduzione per cui sarà necessario aspettare pazientemente che questa operazione finisca. Questa operazione viene fatta solo al primo avvio.

Installazione (formato .zip):
-------------
1) Copiare il file della traduzione nella stessa directory dove risiede il file principale del gioco.
Esempio: Si abbia un gioco "HurryUp" installato in "C:\Giochi\HurryUp". In questa cartella si troverà il file principale del gioco chiamato "HurryUp.exe". (Nota: Nei PC dove non sono mostrate le estensioni dei file noti, questo file risulterà solo "HurryUp" di "Tipo" come "Applicazione").
Così facendo, nella cartella "C:\Giochi\HurryUp" saranno presenti SIA il file principale del gioco CHE quello della traduzione.
2) Scomprimere il file della traduzione.
3) Al termine si potrà cancellare il file della traduzione.
4) Per verificare che la traduzione sia stata installata correttamente, verificare che ci sia il file zzz.rpy nella cartella "game" del gioco (Nel nostro esempio in "C:\Giochi\HurryUp\game") e che ci sia la cartella "it" in "game/tl" (Nel nostro esempio in "C:\Giochi\HurryUp\game\tl").

Manuale:
-------
Un piccolo manuale illustrato con le istruzioni di installazione, in formato .pdf, lo trovate qui: Mega

Segnalazione degli errori:
-------------------------
Qualora il gioco abbia crash/errori/anomalie, prego inviarmi, in privato, i file log.txt, error.txt e traceback.txt che vengono generati nella cartella dove c'è il file eseguibile del gioco (Nota: Non tutti e tre questi file sono sempre presenti) per poter aggiustare le cose...

Attivazione manuale della traduzione:
------------------------------------
Nei giochi dove all'inizio viene imposta la scelta della lingua, l'impostazione di attivazione della lingua italiana viene annullata da questa scelta. Per attivare la traduzione italiana, premere il tasto F12. Se si desidera tornare alla lingua originale del gioco, premere ALT-F12.

F.A.Q:
-----
* I menu' sono in italiano ma i dialoghi in inglese. *
Questa condizione si verifica talvolta quando si utilizza la traduzione in un gioco compresso. Spesso, infatti, la compressione delle immagini del gioco, comporta anche la modifica delle chiavi univoche dei dialoghi rendendo di fatto inutilizzabile la traduzione. I menu' non hanno chiavi univoche e quindi non sono soggetti a questa anomalia.

* Nei dialoghi il genere maschile e femminile sono sbagliati o invertiti. *
L'inglese e' una lingua che accorpa spesso i generi. La frase "Are you tired?" si puo' tradurre sia come "Sei stanca?" che "Sei stanco?". La corretta attribuzione di genere avviene solo analizzando il contesto della frase. I traduttori automatici traducono praticamente sempre al maschile. Sarebbe necessaria una revisione manuense totale, riga per riga, per poter correggere tutti questi errori. Tale lavoro, sia per mole che per tempi, viene considerato troppo gravoso e quindi non viene effettuato. Tuttavia la revisione dei dialoghi attraverso una serie di procedure in rete neurale, attenua questi errori. E' il solo lavoro aggiuntivo che viene posto in essere ed e' cura del traduttore migliorare costantemente queste procedure per affinare sempre' piu' il lavoro.

* I dialoghi di alcuni giochi contengono sigle incomprensibili. *
Putroppo alcuni sviluppatori di giochi utilizzano lo slang nei dialoghi. Tali "storpiature" rendono difficile la traduzione automatica e, spesso, incomprensibili le sigle che, in originale, dovrebbero voler dire qualcosa in forma contratta. In un gioco c'era la sigla "BBRGeem". Nessuno, e ripeto nessuno, dei miei amici americani conosce questa sigla e, soprattutto, il suo significato.

* La traduzione impianta il gioco. *
Prima di fare questa affermazione occorre verificare che il gioco non si impianti nello stesso punto SENZA la traduzione. In questo caso, allora, puo' dipendere da una variabile contenuta del dialogo che, pur avendola "schermata" alla traduzione automatica, questa viene modificata. Una tipica variabile e' il nome del giocatore.

Click to expand...
A lot of people mistake not being able to find certain events as grinding, but this really only happens if you ignore what the game tells you in the beginning and focus on just one character.

Rule of thumb is that new events unlock for every 5 Affection you gain, but progress for many character events is locked to progress with others. No one needs more than 35 Affection right now and that much can be gained in less than 5 minutes of actual stat grinding.

posts.content_html_raw:
Very long post incoming! Just wanted to give my praises/criticisms on the game since I just caught up with the recent update.
So finally catching up with the updates, after god knows how long, I think I'm going to say that Selebus is arguably the most accomplished writer on this site. It's been a real pleasure seeing you take a lot of these stale stock-characters and flip them on our heads by not doing what most would do and just make a ton of gratuitous "subversions," but instead round them out with fluid and fun personalities that let them become their own individuals through rough moments or just really funny situations. There's a lot of ambition and focus, not just in terms of the horror elements and 4th wall breaks, but more so in the little moments and lines where you can see a clear intention to define these characters (in all their pain and pleasure) without having to resort to info dumps or outright saying it. I also appreciate the attention given to upholding the overall themes and structure of the game. Even the most professionally made visual novels have a tendency to lose track of the core of their story by getting sidetracked with things like aesthetic and unique situations that sometimes feel like they're ignoring the cake for the frosting, doubly so for content that's produced on a more serialized or update-driven format. It's very admirable then to see how despite your large cast and expansive world that are both growing more and more, you still are able to tie most things back to the heart of your story and make it so you can go to a lot of different emotional/tonal places while still being grounded. At the end of the day, I can still say that for me this is a story about trauma and pain; how we cope with it, how we work past it, how we relieve it through good and bad means, and how we sometimes bring it on ourselves and others without even knowing it as if it was somehow second nature. That may be simplifying it to a large extent, but I believe that simplicity is a major strength.

There's definitely a strong understanding of character and theme, as well as a confident writing voice that's well-read and personal. There's also a very apparent respect for the genre/culture of Visual Novels despite the motivation to break a lot of its trends. I see a lot of inspiration from Japanese developers like SCA-DI who also like to walk that tight-rope of making H-games that delve into more serious character writing and a hell of a lot of existentialism. For me, that's both this game’s best and worst aspects. Though they can be interesting and profound, the more heady types of VN's have the tendency to get very involved with all of their subversions, meta-textual analysis, and overall philosophizing. If I could describe what I mean in one word, it would have to be indulgence. These types of games are like the "My Dinner with Andre" of eroge where often we end up with so many discussions about topics, but never any action or characterization to tie those ideas together, that eventually the narrative and themes feel more like sophomoric lectures than they do compelling storytelling. LiL doesn't have that level of issue but it's hitting a similar note, mostly due to how many times it repeats its story/character beats. I love moments like the Happy Scenes and more serious events with the girls, but I feel like they're basically saying the same things they said when they first happened, only to then keep repeating that same note every time they pop afterward. For me, it just feels like we never go much of anywhere when the story ramps its tone up, whether that be for horror, drama, or tragic moments. Not in a plot sense, but more in a mood sense. It's always up to level 100 when we take off the "fun-time" glasses, and that's great for hooking people in, but after a while, that level 100 shift becomes easier to adjust to and I feel it weakens the impact of what's trying to be said, especially since the "non-serious" moments are more tonally dynamic in my opinion.

I don't necessarily think this breaks the narrative or anything, but it's what's separating it from good to great for me in terms of the storytelling. Even with the reveals of hard-hitting topics like depression, self-harm, suicide, violence, etc. It can at times feel like the game gets into a sort of predictable rhythm of Dating Sim-Serious Issues-Philosophize-repeat. As I mentioned before, I think it stems more from something like indulgence than like lack of talent or anything bad like that. In fact, I feel like Maya's whole personality shows a bit of self-awareness towards that sort of tendency/want to go on long-winded tangents that basically are different versions of the same points. Most of what I commented on seems more like deliberate choices than mistakes so in all honesty it's really just my personal preference.

There are definitely other aspects of the game I enjoy and/or wish were stronger, but I think story and character are the real heart of this game and I just wanted to give my thoughts on it. Overall I still really do enjoy this game a ton so far, I just think there's definitely room for it to be stronger in some aspects and I criticize only because I appreciate what you do.

Thank you very much for taking the time to both play and critique my game! I completely agree with basically everything you said, and kind of expected to hear this sort of feedback when I was first thinking up LiL. The greatest worry I always have when looking at my writing from a critical perspective is that it's sort of like this formulaic chaos where, just as you mentioned, it becomes a cycle of dramatic mood shifts that start in similar places and end in similar places. Indulgent is a good word, but I feel that there's a bit more to it than that- and all of it comes from the challenges I knew would arise when creating something of this scale.

The key worry for me has been not moving anything drastically forward until everyone has reached a certain...plateau, I guess- as I very much want this to be a story where the class progresses as a whole in tandem with individual character progression. But having so many fucking characters makes that an interesting challenge. I want everyone to progress together, but progressing so many people at once is quite a laborious and lengthy undertaking. And that's not me making an excuse or anything, just trying to explain where I am and where I want to go.

The coming update is easily the biggest in terms of actual main story beats, so I think you'll start seeing some of that indulgence begin to slip away as the direction the game is heading in becomes more apparent. It is, however, important to note that those incessant cycles of good-to bad-to very bad-to very good-to normal-to weird religious philosophy-to sex-back to good will likely never fully go away. One thing I picked up from SCA-DI (Who I'm very excited to see name-dropped in a discussion about my game as he is probably my biggest influence) is that sort of weird, unfiltered/borderline-nonsensical rambling type of prose. It wasn't until I played Subarashiki Hibi that I thought, "You know what? Fuck it. I'm just going to write for myself and if people like it, they like it." So, while I've completely embraced the fact that I just write whatever comes to my mind rather than sitting down and specifically plotting out who is going to dynamically change and when, I completely understand that that exact quality of my work may be a turn-off for some people. I always know where I want to go, but I admittedly might take a little too long to get there at times.

Last thing to note, as I feel it ties directly back into how the horror aspects are circling around to the same ideas is that, to some extent, that's exactly what they're doing. And while it won't be clear or obvious now, each one of them provides a different sort of hint or tidbit of information that will be vital to "connecting the dots" in the future. We're still only in the first part of the game and there are many gigantic reveals that have yet to even almost-surface- but I'm in this for the long-haul. Spoiler:
Some thoughts on the storytelling
So finally catching up with the updates, after god knows how long, I think I'm going to say that Selebus is arguably the most accomplished writer on this site. It's been a real pleasure seeing you take a lot of these stale stock-characters and flip them on our heads by not doing what most would do and just make a ton of gratuitous "subversions," but instead round them out with fluid and fun personalities that let them become their own individuals through rough moments or just really funny situations. There's a lot of ambition and focus, not just in terms of the horror elements and 4th wall breaks, but more so in the little moments and lines where you can see a clear intention to define these characters (in all their pain and pleasure) without having to resort to info dumps or outright saying it. I also appreciate the attention given to upholding the overall themes and structure of the game. Even the most professionally made visual novels have a tendency to lose track of the core of their story by getting sidetracked with things like aesthetic and unique situations that sometimes feel like they're ignoring the cake for the frosting, doubly so for content that's produced on a more serialized or update-driven format. It's very admirable then to see how despite your large cast and expansive world that are both growing more and more, you still are able to tie most things back to the heart of your story and make it so you can go to a lot of different emotional/tonal places while still being grounded. At the end of the day, I can still say that for me this is a story about trauma and pain; how we cope with it, how we work past it, how we relieve it through good and bad means, and how we sometimes bring it on ourselves and others without even knowing it as if it was somehow second nature. That may be simplifying it to a large extent, but I believe that simplicity is a major strength.
There's definitely a strong understanding of character and theme, as well as a confident writing voice that's well-read and personal. There's also a very apparent respect for the genre/culture of Visual Novels despite the motivation to break a lot of its trends. I see a lot of inspiration from Japanese developers like SCA-DI who also like to walk that tight-rope of making H-games that delve into more serious character writing and a hell of a lot of existentialism. For me, that's both this game’s best and worst aspects. Though they can be interesting and profound, the more heady types of VN's have the tendency to get very involved with all of their subversions, meta-textual analysis, and overall philosophizing. If I could describe what I mean in one word, it would have to be indulgence. These types of games are like the "My Dinner with Andre" of eroge where often we end up with so many discussions about topics, but never any action or characterization to tie those ideas together, that eventually the narrative and themes feel more like sophomoric lectures than they do compelling storytelling. LiL doesn't have that level of issue but it's hitting a similar note, mostly due to how many times it repeats its story/character beats. I love moments like the Happy Scenes and more serious events with the girls, but I feel like they're basically saying the same things they said when they first happened, only to then keep repeating that same note every time they pop afterward. It's always up to level 100 when we take off the "fun-time" glasses, and that's great for hooking people in, but after a while, that level 100 shift becomes easier to adjust to and I feel it weakens the impact of what's trying to be said, especially since the "non-serious" moments are more tonally dynamic in my opinion.
I don't necessarily think this breaks the narrative or anything, but it's what's separating it from good to great for me in terms of the storytelling. Even with the reveals of hard-hitting topics like depression, self-harm, suicide, violence, etc. It can at times feel like the game gets into a sort of predictable rhythm of Dating Sim-Serious Issues-Philosophize-repeat. As I mentioned before, I think it stems more from something like indulgence than like lack of talent or anything bad like that. In fact, I feel like Maya's whole personality shows a bit of self-awareness towards that sort of tendency/want to go on long-winded tangents that basically are different versions of the same points. Most of what I commented on seems more like deliberate choices than mistakes so in all honesty it's really just my personal preference.

Overall I still really do enjoy this game a ton so far, I just think there's definitely room for it to be stronger in some aspects and I criticize only because I appreciate what you do.

And that's not me making an excuse or anything, just trying to explain where I am and where I want to go.

The coming update is easily the biggest in terms of actual main story beats, so I think you'll start seeing some of that indulgence begin to slip away as the direction the game is heading in becomes more apparent. I always know where I want to go, but I admittedly might take a little too long to get there at times.

Last thing to note, as I feel it ties directly back into how the horror aspects are circling around to the same ideas is that, to some extent, that's exactly what they're doing. It's always up to level 100 when we take off the "fun-time" glasses, and that's great for hooking people in, but after a while, that level 100 shift becomes easier to adjust to and I feel it weakens the impact of what's trying to be said, especially since the "non-serious" moments are more tonally dynamic in my opinion.

I don't necessarily think this breaks the narrative or anything, but it's what's separating it from good to great for me in terms of the storytelling. I also appreciate the attention given to upholding the overall themes and structure of the game. Even the most professionally made visual novels have a tendency to lose track of the core of their story by getting sidetracked with things like aesthetic and unique situations that sometimes feel like they're ignoring the cake for the frosting, doubly so for content that's produced on a more serialized or update-driven format. It's very admirable then to see how despite your large cast and expansive world that are both growing more and more, you still are able to tie most things back to the heart of your story and make it so you can go to a lot of different emotional/tonal places while still being grounded. At the end of the day, I can still say that for me this is a story about trauma and pain; how we cope with it, how we work past it, how we relieve it through good and bad means, and how we sometimes bring it on ourselves and others without even knowing it as if it was somehow second nature. That may be simplifying it to a large extent, but I believe that simplicity is a major strength.
There's definitely a strong understanding of character and theme, as well as a confident writing voice that's well-read and personal. There's also a very apparent respect for the genre/culture of Visual Novels despite the motivation to break a lot of its trends. I see a lot of inspiration from Japanese developers like SCA-DI who also like to walk that tight-rope of making H-games that delve into more serious character writing and a hell of a lot of existentialism. For me, that's both this game’s best and worst aspects. Though they can be interesting and profound, the more heady types of VN's have the tendency to get very involved with all of their subversions, meta-textual analysis, and overall philosophizing. If I could describe what I mean in one word, it would have to be indulgence. These types of games are like the "My Dinner with Andre" of eroge where often we end up with so many discussions about topics, but never any action or characterization to tie those ideas together, that eventually the narrative and themes feel more like sophomoric lectures than they do compelling storytelling. LiL doesn't have that level of issue but it's hitting a similar note, mostly due to how many times it repeats its story/character beats. I love moments like the Happy Scenes and more serious events with the girls, but I feel like they're basically saying the same things they said when they first happened, only to then keep repeating that same note every time they pop afterward. For me, it just feels like we never go much of anywhere when the story ramps its tone up, whether that be for horror, drama, or tragic moments. Not in a plot sense, but more in a mood sense. It's always up to level 100 when we take off the "fun-time" glasses, and that's great for hooking people in, but after a while, that level 100 shift becomes easier to adjust to and I feel it weakens the impact of what's trying to be said, especially since the "non-serious" moments are more tonally dynamic in my opinion.
I don't necessarily think this breaks the narrative or anything, but it's what's separating it from good to great for me in terms of the storytelling. Even with the reveals of hard-hitting topics like depression, self-harm, suicide, violence, etc. It can at times feel like the game gets into a sort of predictable rhythm of Dating Sim-Serious Issues-Philosophize-repeat. As I mentioned before, I think it stems more from something like indulgence than like lack of talent or anything bad like that. In fact, I feel like Maya's whole personality shows a bit of self-awareness towards that sort of tendency/want to go on long-winded tangents that basically are different versions of the same points. Most of what I commented on seems more like deliberate choices than mistakes so in all honesty it's really just my personal preference.
There are definitely other aspects of the game I enjoy and/or wish were stronger, but I think story and character are the real heart of this game and I just wanted to give my thoughts on it. Overall I still really do enjoy this game a ton so far, I just think there's definitely room for it to be stronger in some aspects and I criticize only because I appreciate what you do.

spoilers.title: Wall of text
spoilers.html: You're doing fine, really. This is easily some of the best character development I've seen in a very long time and that does include some AAA games in the mix of competition. You're not going too fast, the character arcs will catch up to the main pretty quick, nor are you going too slow. If you need more time at some point, we'll understand, at least some of us. If that's what it takes to get it done right, so be it, take an extra month of my money without something in return, I'm giving it to you because I want to anyway, I don't consider it payment for the game, but part of a long list of things I really would love to get done as thanks. In regards to the cycle you mentioned, the whole good to bad to very bad part, that is somewhat necessary in a game like this, I would think, given its nature and that of its genre. As far as your 'write what I want' mentality, that's actually something a lot, and I mean A LOT, of games don't do, especially on the Patreon/SubscribeStar side of things. The majority do exactly as their patrons tell them IF they do anything at all. That's not to say you're the only Patreon/SubscribeStar dev that does as their vision of their project directs them to do, but you are one of a rare breed these days and I most definitely applaud you for that. Feedback is important, of course, but your vision is the most important aspect of any that goes into the project. Without it, the project simply would not exist and we would not be here now. With regards to the formulaic aspect, there's always some sense of that in something like this, it would just be unorganized chaos otherwise. The shifts in mood can be a little jarring, more like emotional whiplash, but that actually adds to the shock value. Nobody but LiL veterans, can we even call ourselves veterans at this stage, expects that kind of thing and it really adds to what you're going for. You'veseen it in the thread, the complaints and the comments about how people didn't expect something or were emotionally impacted by something in a way they didn't expect, need I remind you of the talk about the event "Bluejay" earlier in the thread? Seriously, while I was not expecting that to happen with that character this early, it did and it had one of the greatest effects on me in the game so far second only to Rin's issues because they were over a longer period of time and had time to sink in while "Bluejay" was pretty much an instant in the game instead of a whole series of events. I'm not alone in that, either. Several of us were affected. I mean "Bluejay definitely had the best shock value because it happened so fast, that's for sure, but Rin's episode. That creepy smile as she holds up her shirt to flash Sensei is burned into my memory for a VERY different reason than her boobs. I'm not going to forget that for a very long time IF I do at all.

posts.content_html_raw:
May contains some spoilers about the early scenes in the game. Please play the game.


After my first interaction with a Happy scene which left a deep scar, I TRIED to keep on playing but ALWAYS expected the worst to come...
In the end, I finally stopped playing for a short while out of fear. (Damn these clocks)

Questioning why was I afraid of a "simple" and "childish" video game, the next IRL day, I ended up doing a FULL 180* and went ahead and said: FUCK IT and played some more. But my perspective of the game had already been forever altered...
After my little petty rush of pride was gone, everything about the game had been changed in the worst of ways...

EVERY single click had so much pressure on it. What if I triggered another one of those scenes? What if I get jumped scare?
I was LEGIT scared.
Every morning that Ami would loudly knock on my door I'd get a short drawback that brought me to my initial fear of the game. I vaguely remember when the MC quoted (when talking about Ami in the early stages of the game): "She looks so defenseless and pure, it makes me want to absolutely destroy her protect her". I looked away from the screen and stared at the wall in awe... how the hell was that game taking me on this fked up rollercoaster of stress and panic.

Once again, as I feared, a second Happy scene happened, but this time was expected! (=D) I decided against my all being to not hide behind my hands and watched the whole scene play out...and it honestly wasn't so bad...STILL weird and fked up on many levels, but not as bad as I thought.

I think that was the exact moment when I decided to stop being afraid and questioning the intentions of this game and to ACTUALLY enjoy this with full intent to witness those "happy" scenes.

I understand that there is ABSOLUTELY more to come and that I have probably not even scratch the lid of this game yet. But I gotta say I've never felt this way about ANY other game. I WANT to experience this game and let it take me on a weird twisted ride to my demise (Yea that was edgy my bad) but seriously this game is weirdly addictive...I watched a H-scene for the sake of the plot and I am now SKIPPING the repeatable scene for the sake of grinding the lust factor just to see some MORE scenes!

I really can't explain as much as I would like to, cause I can't even understand these weird feelings that this game is forcibly making me go through. I HIGHLY suggest that you play this game yourself and join me in this. I haven't even play that much yet but trust me after this post I'm spending some quality hours on it!

TL: DR This game takes you on a twisted and beautiful reality ride with no seatbelt.
Quick thx to alex2011 who is a kind dude for indirectly pushing me to give this game 1 more go

Selebus I fully support what you do, but I don't know if I love you or hate you as of yet xD

posts.content_html_raw:
Very interesting update, the effort really shows in this one. I wonder how the dev is feeling about the scope of this game, since apparently we're still in "Act 1" and there is at the very least one more to come. I truly hope that working on a single major project for this long doesn't cause burnout or feelings of monotony.

Concerning the new events, I'm glad we get some concrete answers to a few major questions (at least ones that I had). For example, the green scarf, which was mentioned multiple times before. Apparently Maya is the girl who wore the scarf and experienced those memories.

I very much wonder if this "new sensei" that happened to be the one we play as is the same person/personality that Maya remembers from those memories of happier times.

It isn't clear if the person in the new happy event is "old sensei". Not 100% confident on this one, but the "new sensei" remembers the scarf from happy event #7 (hexadecimal text).
And I'm going to guess that Maya refers to herself as the girl with the worst luck in the world is because her lover commited suicide and then the world started resetting, her being the only one remembering it, and their sensei now acts like her old partner with memory loss.

All these hypotheses individually seem very likely to be true (to me at least), but put together like this in a unified theory does make it seem quite the stretch. I'm guessing i only got it partially correct (at best).

Other than that, it also clears up some questions about the three gods/users, and their roles/characteristics.

I also empathize with the herculean effort it took to pull Zonghli.

The joke about the connection between sensei and santa was comedic gold. I didn't expect it in the slightest and i'm amazed Selebus managed to come up with it. I'm sure it's just personal preference but, damn if it wasn't the best joke I've heard in months.
In fact, the entire event was hilarious. So many moments captured some raw feeling behind the words, almost like i could see the scenes play out live in my head like a movie, with emotive expressions and sound, instead of the still images on a windowed program that they actually were. ("FOR IRELAND")

All in all, definitely one of the best updates in memory. If anyone new was wondering if they should play the game, this would be a decent time to start imo.

JohnnyRazer said:
Well, that's almost my point. I see it like she either grew emotionally dumb over so many cycles or intentionally shut in, or maybe both. Click to expand...
She isn't totally emotionless since she does seem to bear negative emotions toward player Sensei, though these emotions are not as strong as Yumi's outright hatred of player Sensei and don't seem to be truly negative, just defensively so to distance herself. She definitely shut herself off from everyone emotionally, but why is what we still have to figure out. To make someone do something that drastic, it takes A LOT. The human spirit isn't so easily broken, so it must have been something horrific that caused her to do this. The loss of a loved one in an accident or murder, perhaps, which is where old Sensei comes in. We see in the opening that something happens to Sensei at one point, but we don't know who witnessed it or who caused it if anyone other than him was involved. This leaves open the possibility that old Sensei either killed himself for yet another unknown reason or that he was murdered and this took place essentially right in front of Maya, not with the perpetrator in view, but most definitely with Sensei in view. By the time she could have gotten help, he would be dead. By the time she could have rushed to the site of the incident, he would be dead. By the time she got to where he, and the potential murderer, was, he would be dead. This would lead to utter despair, a feeling of hopelessness so great that the mind has to do something to protect her, it has to shut off her emotions so it cannt happen again. If it does, she's going to break and break hard. We're talking totally unresponsive, off in her own little world permanently, maybe mumbling utter nonsense. She remains in this 'protected' state even through the resets since she is apparently immune to them like player Sensei is, by which I mean they both have full memory of the things that happened before and during, but the others do not have any memory from before the point the reset brought them back to. In other words, what we see from Maya isn't truly an inability to show emotion or lack of emotion, but an act, a facade to keep her distance so she doesn't have to bear that pain again. When she sees the scarf, it could have broken that facade for a bit. With enough emotion welling up, not even the best actress on the planet can hide it.

She essentially fits a small gap between two different anime tropes, the kuudere and the tsundere. She gets the kuudere for her stoic nature, since kuuderes show little to no emotion except around the one they love, which as I said may not be her real personality given the early scenes that appear to be of her prior to the Sensei shift, and the tsundere for her constant bashing of Sensei. So, this is my theory about Maya and sensei.

Our mc is the old sensei indeed, he just doesn't remember about it. Maya said sensei had a lot of different personalities along with the many resets the world had. I think she was in love with the original sensei personality, after his death, she grieved a lot, and with some unknown way she reseted the world the first time. The problem is that, after she reseted the world, and sensei was alive again, she realized he lost his memories and even his personality was a little different. Even if he wasn't exactly the same person she felt in love with, she still tried to have a relationship with him, and make him become the person he used to be again. The problem is that the reset would come again and again, until she just grew tired of this cycle. Then Maya just convinced herself that all her effort was pointless, because sensei would never be the same person again, and would even forget everything after a new cycle of resets. This resulted in the Maya we know now, that try her best to ignore her feelings and think sensei existence is just disgusting. What Maya didn't expect is that this time, things are happening different from the other times. Now sensei is starting to remember things from the past, he's even starting to act like the original sensei, like giving her the green scarf, wich I presume was a gift only the original sensei ever gave her.

Well, my theory is probably wrong, but this is just one of the things I love about this game. The events are just so umpredictible, that we always have a surprise in each update. At this point Selebus is by far, one of my favorites devs in the site, and I hope people starts to notice this game even more and it becomes one of the biggest games around here.

spoilers.html: Our mc is the old sensei indeed, he just doesn't remember about it. Maya said sensei had a lot of different personalities along with the many resets the world had. I think she was in love with the original sensei personality, after his death, she grieved a lot, and with some unknown way she reseted the world the first time. The problem is that, after she reseted the world, and sensei was alive again, she realized he lost his memories and even his personality was a little different. Even if he wasn't exactly the same person she felt in love with, she still tried to have a relationship with him, and make him become the person he used to be again. The problem is that the reset would come again and again, until she just grew tired of this cycle. Then Maya just convinced herself that all her effort was pointless, because sensei would never be the same person again, and would even forget everything after a new cycle of resets. This resulted in the Maya we know now, that try her best to ignore her feelings and think sensei existence is just disgusting. What Maya didn't expect is that this time, things are happening different from the other times. Now sensei is starting to remember things from the past, he's even starting to act like the original sensei, like giving her the green scarf, wich I presume was a gift only the original sensei ever gave her.

I started playing it probably 10 or 15 times. But it's like an anime... First it's the number of cuties that gets your attention, then it's the shitty plot that ruins it.
All the little things aside, it's the same here, every time I play for the sake of cuties and find the dialogues (exactly the dialogues when two or more people talk) very interesting and enjoyable, I don't mind a long story and long relationship development at all...
But... every time I run into the same problem.... what age is the game meant for? because i have a strong impression that the game is written by a 15 year old girl for 15 year old girls. Because...
The in-between monologues and these "happy" inserts such idiocy, such a waste of time... stupid, pseudo-religious bullshit... and then there's this complicated thing about developing a relationship with the girls...
I thought, "okay, you can skip all that for the sex scenes with the cuties," but then I ran into a problem, too.

I think you're doing either "softcore" or "hardcore" or something in between, but mixing it up is ridiculous.
I have terrible mixed feelings about this novel, but considering that it's a porn game, I would say that the impression is rather negative.

If you chose to finger blast Chika before Rin got her chance, regardless of circumstances, you were a bad homie. That's the meaning of the term bad homie in the context of this game. Yes, she has her roommate, Futaba, but Futaba alone would not be enough at this level, not with this much damage done. Rin would feel far too betrayed to trust even her.

The reason they call it a visual novel is because it is a computerized novel with visual aids. It is a text medium with pictures, the text is ALWAYS the focus of the developer behind the novel except in instances where sex is thrown in just to have sex scenes. No, there is not plenty of information in the visuals, you could have a rape scene depicted and have the text say it was consensual. In this, admittedly very extreme, example, the act is not a rape scene because the text says she consented. The reverse is also possible, the visual looks consensual, but in the text she resists, so it is rape. ViA visual aid does not transform the medium. A physical novel, by which I mean an actual book, doesn't become a visual medium just because it was published with some pictures in it, so a visual novel doesn't either. There are plenty of physical novels that, yes, have pictures, usually an illustration at the beginning of a chapter if anything unless it is adapted from a film, in which case actual scenes from the film might be placed on inserted photo paper. Things are already balanced exactly as Selebus wants, with the text taking priority. 'too much text' is NEVER a valid argument in anything short of a school assignment with a maximum word limit.
Click to expand...
Bruh, comic books are analyzed as visual medium and understood as such, you can tell a story with zero text and only visuals. Can you argue in good faith that comics/manga are visual medium, but vn are not? I can't. I can't exactly tell you where is a cut off point between a textual and visual mediums, what ratio of text to picture it is, but vn are definitely visual medium.

"Too much text" is absolutely a valid argument, if it wasn't there will be no editing. If it doesn't serve any valid purpose, cut it out. There's a meme going around, that the "left can't meme" or whatever. It usually goes with examples of such butched attempts, with walls of text attached. I understand, that's a bit reaching, but if enything mems are visual mediums, they require the least amount of text.

Visual part in vn goes beyond "aid", it's a parallel avenue of telling a story, and in Lessons of Love there are many examples of "showing, but not telling", in other words delivering information exclusively through visual means.

The "too much text" argument isn't about overall word count. You have an impression that there's too much text if it doesn't do anything for you. It repeats things that are already said, establish already established things, doesn't do anything for characters or story etc. It's entirely subjective, but it's there.

If you keep hearing "there's too much _blank_" in your story, movie, whatever, even if medium that you use to tell said story relies heavily on this _blank_ to the point of being defined as a medium by this thing, it's time to tweak things around, shorten this a and that, smart it up, change the way you deliver this piece of info, if it's important, or cut it away if it's not. This apply to anything, be it books or movies.

Even in my response I cut things away, that I deemed unimportant, or too poorly worded to be meaningful and broke it down by paragraphs to make it somewhat easier to read. I bet you did that too with your answer. Because "too much" is still too much.

For what it's worth, I don't agree it's a betrayal if you don't know beforehand how Rin feels. I know you don't agree and that's fine. You're entitled to your opinion. But I think you're really downplaying the following aspects

1.) There is a path that you can engage with Chika BEFORE you know Rin is into her.
2.) There is no indication before you start Schadenfreude that it will go down the path it does.
3.) Once you realize where Schadenfreude is going, you have no choices to stop except to load a old save (or rollback if you're not too far into it).
4.) If you haven't made the promise to Rin and she hasn't told her your feelings, you have no reason to stop. This event might not be required for the beach event but it is required in general to progress. And neither of these things can be known by a first time player.
5.) Comparing this to real life is a bad comparison because a game cannot possibly address all the different aspects and choices a real person can make in this situation.

All that being said, Selebus has said that the intent is to be unfair here. That you are meant to fail in situations like this. So if that is the intent, then so be it. The events play out like this. You find out Rin is bi (Event: Rin's Secret). You find out she has a crush on Chika (Event: Cafe Mocha).

At this point, it would be common sense not to go after Chika as a courtesy to Rin. She specifically says "Oh, and don't try to steal her from me either! I see the way you look at her sometimes!" and "Still! At least keep your hands off of her until she properly rejects me!" (Event: Cafe Mocha). These are the quotes which warn you NOT to make a move on Chika, this was the in game warning that several people seem to have missed because they didn't play this event.

Rin begins to have issues, this is also the first appearance of the miserable Rin model, which is the one with the dark bags under her eyes for when she has issues currently going on, usually because of lack of sleep, a week of no sleep in the case of this event (Event: Nothing Was Missing, Except Me).

She has a full blown breakdown into a state of delirium so bad that she flashes you when she normally wouldn't and practically screamed you out of the room the last time you walked in on her in less than full clothing, which was in the event Boundaries. This boob flash is accompanied by a creepy smile that still haunts me to this day. You also find out she's been cutting her wrists, in other words, self harming. Sensei does state that the marks aren't fresh, but I don't believe that to be the case, not when she's delirious and not with as dark as they are. They aren't from within the last hour or so, but they are recent. (Event: Delirium).

Rin has an encounter with Chika where Chika tells Rin she's cute, Rin takes this as a sign of there being a chance (Event: Sock Fetish).

On to the main point in question, the beach event. During a prior conversation to the confession, Chika hints at having someone she likes and Rin comes to talk to Sensei with tears in her eyes, basically having already figured out who this person Chika likes is. She also hots every nail on the head when guessing how far player Sensei has gone with Chika if the player has seen Schadenfreude, and yes, she breaks down into crying because player Sensei, and the player by extension, hurt her and player Sensei does admit to it. Rin sits with Chika on the beach that same night for the talk that would determine where their relationship goes, whether it stays simple friendship or mutual love. During that talk, Rin is so nervous that she takes the leap of faith without easing Chika into it, leaving Chika speechless. Rin takes this as a no despite no real answer being given, which it later turns out is the case. She cries her heart out in Sensei's room afterwards and sleeps in his room. She disappears at one point, having left for home early, not to be seen until after the beach trip is over (Events: Smile Guide and Cry. Cry. Cry. in that order).

IF the player did do Schadenfreude before the beach event, Rin will appear at the cafe later, eyes puffy once again. This appearance at the cafe happens no matter what, but what happens during this event is what Schadenfreude changes, not her appearing at the cafe in the first place. She goes on a, slightly deranged, tangent about how she thinks about what it's like for player Sensei and Chika to be together, what player Sensei and Chika do together when alone, and about a dream she had where, foreshadowing alert, she found a new world with a reset button she would press until Chika loved her instead, which is the definition of insanity, by the way. At this point, IF Schadenfreude was triggered, despite her earlier statement about not getting mad, you can tell she's only hiding her anger because she constantly takes shots at player Sensei throughout the event. She admits to getting turned on by this dream she had, the one stated earlier, and almost rubbing against player Sensei, but then remembering his betrayal, the player's betrayal, killed her arousal. (Event: Nothing Was Different).

She can then be found in her dorm with Futaba, where she is stated to have gotten a text from Chika she refuses to reply to. She's scared, probably more than she has ever been at any other point in her life. Chika used three very specific words in this text, words that almost never bode well, "Can we talk?" was all it said. This text tormented her, pushed her even further into depression, but at least she didn't suffer another delirium episode (Event: Two Steps Back).

She has enough of trying to get a hold of her by text in this event and actually comes to her room. Player Sensei leaves at the request of Chika, but we get to see the conversation they have. Chika gives Rin the closure she needs, a proper rejection. (Event: Ten Steps Forward). If you failed to heed the warnings in Cafe Mocha, Ten Steps Forward is Rin's last event so far IF the player gets any further in the case of a betrayal.

Oh boy was that painful to watch again, lasting emotional impact is a great sign, well done Selebus. Editing is often more about mistakes than too many words and in only one case does editing involve a slimming down of the word count, when there is a maximum word count limit involved.
ALL text in a visual novel or any other text medium serves a purpose or it would not be there.

spoilers.html:
The events play out like this. You find out Rin is bi (Event: Rin's Secret). You find out she has a crush on Chika (Event: Cafe Mocha).

At this point, it would be common sense not to go after Chika as a courtesy to Rin. She specifically says "Oh, and don't try to steal her from me either! I see the way you look at her sometimes!" and "Still! At least keep your hands off of her until she properly rejects me!" (Event: Cafe Mocha). These are the quotes which warn you NOT to make a move on Chika, this was the in game warning that several people seem to have missed because they didn't play this event.

Rin begins to have issues, this is also the first appearance of the miserable Rin model, which is the one with the dark bags under her eyes for when she has issues currently going on, usually because of lack of sleep, a week of no sleep in the case of this event (Event: Nothing Was Missing, Except Me).

She has a full blown breakdown into a state of delirium so bad that she flashes you when she normally wouldn't and practically screamed you out of the room the last time you walked in on her in less than full clothing, which was in the event Boundaries. This boob flash is accompanied by a creepy smile that still haunts me to this day. You also find out she's been cutting her wrists, in other words, self harming. Sensei does state that the marks aren't fresh, but I don't believe that to be the case, not when she's delirious and not with as dark as they are. They aren't from within the last hour or so, but they are recent. (Event: Delirium).

Rin has an encounter with Chika where Chika tells Rin she's cute, Rin takes this as a sign of there being a chance (Event: Sock Fetish).

On to the main point in question, the beach event. During a prior conversation to the confession, Chika hints at having someone she likes and Rin comes to talk to Sensei with tears in her eyes, basically having already figured out who this person Chika likes is. She also hots every nail on the head when guessing how far player Sensei has gone with Chika if the player has seen Schadenfreude, and yes, she breaks down into crying because player Sensei, and the player by extension, hurt her and player Sensei does admit to it. Rin sits with Chika on the beach that same night for the talk that would determine where their relationship goes, whether it stays simple friendship or mutual love. During that talk, Rin is so nervous that she takes the leap of faith without easing Chika into it, leaving Chika speechless. Rin takes this as a no despite no real answer being given, which it later turns out is the case. She cries her heart out in Sensei's room afterwards and sleeps in his room. She disappears at one point, having left for home early, not to be seen until after the beach trip is over (Events: Smile Guide and Cry. Cry. Cry. in that order).

IF the player did do Schadenfreude before the beach event, Rin will appear at the cafe later, eyes puffy once again. This appearance at the cafe happens no matter what, but what happens during this event is what Schadenfreude changes, not her appearing at the cafe in the first place. She goes on a, slightly deranged, tangent about how she thinks about what it's like for player Sensei and Chika to be together, what player Sensei and Chika do together when alone, and about a dream she had where, foreshadowing alert, she found a new world with a reset button she would press until Chika loved her instead, which is the definition of insanity, by the way. At this point, IF Schadenfreude was triggered, despite her earlier statement about not getting mad, you can tell she's only hiding her anger because she constantly takes shots at player Sensei throughout the event. She admits to getting turned on by this dream she had, the one stated earlier, and almost rubbing against player Sensei, but then remembering his betrayal, the player's betrayal, killed her arousal. (Event: Nothing Was Different).

She can then be found in her dorm with Futaba, where she is stated to have gotten a text from Chika she refuses to reply to. She's scared, probably more than she has ever been at any other point in her life. Chika used three very specific words in this text, words that almost never bode well, "Can we talk?" was all it said. This text tormented her, pushed her even further into depression, but at least she didn't suffer another delirium episode (Event: Two Steps Back).

Next is another dorm event, she is on her laptop when you enter the room, eyes still puffy. Chika is still texting, trying to get to Rin. She has enough of trying to get a hold of her by text in this event and actually comes to her room. Player Sensei leaves at the request of Chika, but we get to see the conversation they have. Chika gives Rin the closure she needs, a proper rejection. (Event: Ten Steps Forward). If you failed to heed the warnings in Cafe Mocha, Ten Steps Forward is Rin's last event so far IF the player gets any further in the case of a betrayal.

With the logic you are using, you shouldn't pursue ANY of the girls at all. Were there hints that something was off with Rin? Sure. But I read every word and did not pick up on Rin having feelings for Chika. Does that make my oblivious? Maybe. But people don't always pick up on hints or read them in the right way. It turned out it was the probably quite early "The Letter T" event, it just didn't occur to me to select the choice leading to it. I don't know what's the soonest you can trigger it, but since another event that depends on it is listed at day 102+, it took me at least double time. And I don't think it was entirely my fault either. Sure, it was me who missed it, but there's quite a lot of choices, so it can easily happen when hunting for the one that moves you forward, when you have no idea in advance when and where it will be.

I'm not really complaining, just saying that things may be obvious to hardcore fans who know the game inside and out, but not so much to everyone else.
Click to expand...
There is no 'right order' to play in, there is no requirement unless a prerequisite is involved, however, it is still the player's responsibility when their actions, or lack thereof in some cases, cause a negative outcome. The general rule of thumb for this game is to progress each girl in case a character event is a prerequisite to a main event, of which there are multiple cases, including the beach event. In doing so, you would trigger Cafe Mocha and would, by extension, learn of Rin's crush and the warnings she gives.

You don't have to read 200+ pages, top right, there's a search function. Plus this issue is the most talked about issue in the entire game, so it is likely to appear on nearly every other page of the thread, not just a select few of the 200+. By the way, apparently my name is now no one because I did exactly that, several times, without the search function. I've spent hours on this thread combing for answers alone.

It is very easy to do it wrong, you're right, but it is even easier to do it right. It only takes knowledge gained from a single event. Yes, there are multiple triggers involving specific character events, which are events for specific girls. There is a trigger list in this thread, I would suggest reading it for proof of this.

The natural choice is to do what gives the best outcome for the girl you want. In the case of Rin, that means not playing Chika's Schadenfreude event before the beach event is over. If you, collective you, miss the warnings because you didn't play the event, you chose to do so, making it your fault she was betrayed. There are multiple events like this, where you can miss them for not doing something, this just happens to be the most talked about of the bunch. Most lust events can be missed as well if you fail to grind the lust stat high enough in time and most first lust events serve as a lockout for future lust events. In all cases above, it was the player's decision that led to missing the event, so yes, the player and only the player can and should bear the blame.

Spending more time than necessary to unlock events is a consequence of not doing certain things, events that serve as prerequisites in the case you, personal you this time, presented.

There is only one person in this thread who knows the game inside and out, even the 'hardcore fans' are just along for the ride. That one person is Selebus himself.

posts.content_html_raw:
One other note in regards to whether or not the player should face consequences for something that isn't explicitly indicated will result in consequences.

A lot of games I would agree, but in this one it shouldn't take a rocket scientist to realize that a teacher fingering his students can, will, and should cause unintended consequences. I'm not sure you can even describe them as unintended with how irresponsible and immoral sensei is. Being a bad homie is honestly the least of the fallout he will likely be facing a few events down the road.

Yeah you can argue it's a game and as the protagonist we can expect to act in certain ways that make sense in world even if they'd get him jailed for life or killed in the real world, but this game in particular is very clear that it's going to screw with that specific perspective even as it encourages it.

That and if the game was explicit about things, most of us would have acted as good homies (which sensei clearly is not intended to be at the moment) and would have missed one of the most emotionally jarring and well written scenes in the game.

Just keep multiple saves. I have a "moral" save where sensei has listened to Maya about his niece and was a good homie, and another save where he takes every sex scene the moment it becomes available. I'm honestly impressed with how Selebus has woven the development of the game itself into how the story unfolds, personally.

posts.content_html_raw:
Ok, so, when I got this game I just saw a shitty demo from a community member from a weird place on the internet, and decided to give it a try since the last 4chan game I played was pretty good. But... This game really blew away my expectations (I think I'm using that phrase correctly?). It's good, like really good. I'm not yet done with it, but I'm having a blast.

It's not often I see a piece of work with both soul and meaning, and fun to boot (Another phrase of questionable usage properness). It's been one hell of a long time since a game has had me play it with a hex translator on the side. The characters are great, but special props (I blame bot my usage of unfamiliar terms and this weird typing quirk on slight sleep deprivation) to Maya who, despite me chasing every other girl and supposedly disliking it from the beginning, made me realize a trillion hours into the game how I've looked for her everywhere every time something significant or disturbing happened in the hopes I could discuss it with her, unexpectedly engraving herself into my unconscious as my... something. Solace? Ally? No idea. As someone I wanted to be with.

So yeah, this game speaks to me and I'm enjoying it a lot. I will stick around, please keep up the good work.

P.S. I noticed the apparently controversial homie discussion and I had to say that its existence is great. She didn't need to make me promise not to move on her crush for me to know not to bang my friend's crush. I'm glad I didn't know about it before experiencing it cuz that emotional turmoil and self-restraint made the payoff way worth it. The fact that there was no "don't do this, it will make her sad" or "remember your promise" choice, made the actual choice of no chasing the girl even more real. Not everything choice needs a prompt, nor every consequence needs a warning.

posts.content_html_raw:
Also it's a betrayal because Rin shouldn't have to ask her teacher, no matter how chummy he is with his students, not to finger her best friend who is also her age.

Sensei is an adult teacher. If you were a teenager who was into someone and you found out your friend was already with that person, that's shitty but ultimately you probably both get over it after some yelling and/or ghosting. If you found out your teacher who you had opened up to about your mental illness was with that person it's a completely different level of emotional response.

Rin has no reason to believe Sensei would actually have any sort of sexual relations with a student, so even if she doesn't specifically ask you not to go after Chika she has every right to feel upset, furious, even disgusted (and yes, especially betrayed!) if and when she finds out he did. Because of his position and age there is no reason she should specifically have to ask Sensei to stay away from her crush until she gets a shot.

That's why she doesn't seem to know how to react when she does find out. She's completely blindsided. The one advantage she had in confessing to Chika was that there wasn't supposed to be any competition, then she finds out the one adult she trusted with her mental illness and sexual identity didn't trust her enough to at least give her the heads up that he was interested in Chika.

Yes it's a game and the gameplay loop pushes us to sleep with the students to unlock more scenes, but this genre uses that inherent reward loop of nonsensical behavior as a trap by introducing real world consequences (which as I said before, Sensei has gotten off extremely lightly for his behavior so far).

If you want to follow the "best" route then keep multiple saves and be more careful in the future, it isn't the last trap Selebus is going to lay by a long shot.

Personally I like it. I usually don't have the stones to play as anything but the (horny) goody two shoes so I miss out on this sort of content. I love that Selebus uses gameplay reward loops to trap us into negative scenes because they end up being brilliantly written.
